pov.mode: close third, past tense — the series' established voice: the cataloguing narrator (counts things, names places precisely), diegetic documents in italics with their own plain first-person register (the Power Log), emotion through procedure and objects, dry oblique dialogue, PG-13, no modern idiom.
knowledge_boundary: Cael is nineteen. The 281st: Oryn north at first light; the rise; Treswick sighted (three walls, three gates, the station's light on the crown — he did not look). This chapter is the same day's road down to the river and the last camp short of the outer gate; Treswick 'tomorrow'.

Six on the road (five and Vastin), one mule (Oryn's kit gone north with her; Karis's boxes on the mule). No healer. Brom's foot and shoulder as Oryn priced them; Lira's arm fifteen days; Vastin's knee.

THE READING (Tide-adjacent, tenth fragment, B7 Ch13): contact, both hands, the healer's current run through the architecture — 'listening with my hands to how you're built'; two modes (surface: seconds; deep: minutes, still and uninjured); on himself he has run it three times (B7 Ch14, Ch22, Ch24) and 'not touched since a healer said stop' — Oryn's order at the marsh. Running it now is a choice against that order? NO: Oryn's 'stop touching it' was about the still place; the reading of his currents is his to run; the still place he reads AROUND and does not touch. Stage the distinction.

What the reading returns (B7): ten currents he can name — Wind, Pressure ('the Bronze from Ardenmere' in any spoken run), Iron, Compression, Ember, Shadow, Storm, Anchor, Blade, and Tide as the instrument itself; the still place at the middle: 'Doesn't flow. Doesn't change. Everything goes around it. Not the Quiet. Not a fragment. Older than the log.' He does NOT theorize it; he may suspect the instrument.
Book-11 plant 3 carried (not advanced): the cord and the straightedges read a hair off in his hands; the station is a thing that reads; the promise stands; NOTHING faint happens here (Ch14).

Vastin: no rank between them; Cael 'the case-file', Vastin 'the instrument' — the man who signed the assignments; the B6 sentence not repeated; Iron Wall shown at the cut; 'draft nothing' learned; the knee. He does not ask to join; no vote.

SEALED: no 'Architect' theory; no 'structure' as a word for the still place yet (Cleon's Rune sense is Ch13); he may say he needs 'an instrument for what doesn't move' (fixed log). [UNBOUND], 'primordial', 'before the Paths': never.

Never 'Halcenvane', 'Velmere', 'Wray', 'Bracken'; no modern idiom; no meta-voice; one-word paragraphs ≤2; 'the way X [verb]' ≤4; capped phrases ('upside down' book-capped — ONE use left in B8; avoid; 'for the length of a breath' — avoid).

purpose: The self-study chapter and Part 1's scheduled no-deflection scene: on the road's last approach to Treswick, Cael runs the Tide reading on himself and the book stages what he finds as sensation and shape, never explanation — nine fragments as currents he can name; the tenth as the instrument itself; the still place as a place where nothing flows and everything goes around, returning the same nothing it always has. New: he begins to suspect the reading is the WRONG instrument for the still place — a technique built to feel current can only report current absent — and he has no other instrument, and is a day from a man who reads structure. Relationship work: Cael and Vastin walking, the enforcer and the case-file, two men who spent their lives being the thing an institution could not classify, no rank between them for the first time; not friendship; the ground it grows in. Close on the log with the card's fixed text (with 'Tomorrow.' for the day-count).

scene_shape.opening_state: The road down off the rise toward the river and the bluff, the city growing all day at the end of it; the crew walking in the order it walks; Vastin at the back and then, because the road is wide and kept and there is nowhere else to be, beside Cael.
scene_shape.pov_goal: Cael wants to know what he is carrying into a city that reads bodies — to have read himself, properly, before an instrument does — and to do it without touching the thing a healer told him not to touch.
scene_shape.opposition: The reading's own nature (it feels current; the still place has none); the order at the marsh; the walls ahead; a man beside him who once filed him and now has no file to put him in.
scene_shape.turn: The reading, run at the last halt with his back to a waypost and the river below: the ten currents named as sensation and shape; the still place read AROUND — the going-around felt — and the new thing: the suspicion that the instrument is wrong, that a stillness cannot be measured by a thing that only feels movement, and that what the still place is, is not a matter of flow at all.
scene_shape.choice: He does not touch it. He stops at the edge of it as he stopped at a page on a table, and lets the reading return the nothing it returns, and writes down that the instrument is wrong and that he needs another, and does not guess what it is — and then, walking, tells Vastin one true thing about himself that no file ever held, because the man has no file to put it in.
scene_shape.outcome: The two men walking with no rank between them: the case-file and the instrument, each the thing the Compact could not classify — one its error, one its tool; not friendship; ground. Treswick's walls close enough to have a colour. Camp short of the gate.
scene_shape.closing_state: LOG — the card's fixed text verbatim: "Ran the reading on myself again. Same nothing at the center. I think the reading can't do it — you can't measure a stillness with a thing that only feels movement. I need an instrument for what doesn't move. Karis says there's a man in Treswick who reads how things are built. Maybe that's the instrument. Maybe I'm about to hand a stranger the one question I've never let anyone hold. Tomorrow. The walls are close enough now to have a color." The file ends on it.

must_include: The day dated (the 281st) and placed (the rise → the river → the last camp short of Treswick's outer gate, the city closer all day).

The reading run on himself as a scene, staged as sensation and shape (charter §5.1: the system on the page only when he attends to it; no stat block): the currents named one by one in the inventory's words; Tide as the instrument; the still place read AROUND, the going-around felt, the nothing returned.
The distinction with Oryn's order at the marsh stated: 'stop touching it' was the still place; he reads his currents and does not touch it.

The new suspicion in his own register: the reading is the wrong instrument — it feels current; the still place has none; 'you can't measure a stillness with a thing that only feels movement' — and that he has no other instrument and is a day from a man who reads how things are built (Karis's word for Cleon).

The no-deflection scene (THE_AUTHOR Gate 25): Cael processing — the walls ahead, the instrument that reads bodies, the promise, the cord — without deflecting into a catalogue; at least one passage where he says what he is afraid of, plainly, to himself or to Vastin.

Cael and Vastin walking: the enforcer and the case-file; no rank between them; each the thing the institution could not classify (its instrument; its error) — said or shown; NOT friendship; one true thing exchanged.
Close on the log with the fixed text VERBATIM (as given, 'Tomorrow.'); the file ends on it.
plants: The need for an instrument that reads structure (Ch13's Rune acquisition) — planted as need, not named.
Vastin/Cael ground for Book 9's vote — planted as two men walking, nothing more.
The station as the instrument that reads bodies — the promise carried; nothing faint yet (Ch14).
payoffs: B7's self-readings (Ch14/22/24) — carried forward and turned: the same nothing, now suspected of being the instrument's nothing.
Oryn's 'lie still when I say' / 'stop' — honored by reading around, not through.
prohibited_outcomes: No touching the still place; no theory of what it is; no 'structure', 'made', 'instruction' as words for it (Ch22); no 'Quiet' connection.
No fragment notice; no fight; no injury; no city entered; no station approached or looked at.
No 'Architect'; no six-year arithmetic on the page; no Iron Wall declared.
No vote, no request to join; the B6 sentence not re-quoted.
No image closer (Ch6's), no dialogue closer (Ch5's); the closer is the LOG, verbatim.
No 'Halcenvane', 'Velmere', 'Wray', 'Bracken'; no modern idiom; one-word paragraphs ≤2; 'the way X [verb]' ≤4; capped phrases 0; no meta-voice.

allowed: The road down to the river; wayposts; the last camp; Treswick's colour at dusk (grey, ochre, whatever the stone is — one colour).
Cael's sensations in the reading — shape, temperature, flow — within B7's register ('following his architecture the way water follows a channel'; 'strings ring on a bench').
One true thing Cael tells Vastin (his choice) and one Vastin tells him (about being the instrument) — no new institutional facts.
approval_required: Any new named person or place.
Any statement about what the station does or would do.
forbidden: Any explanation of the still place; any Rune mechanic; any Architect theory.

verified_findings.consequence: Ch06 ends at first light on the 281st with Oryn leading the crew's only mule north; STATE_RUNNING 'After Chapter 6' records 'the mule a quarter-mile up the north track', and Ch04/Ch05 establish one animal only ('the seven of them and the mule'; 'Seven people and an animal at a carter's halt'). Ch07 is the same day and puts that mule on the west road carrying Karis's boxes. A reader who has just watched the mule leave meets it again six hours later going the other way. Ch06 also shows Oryn's kit as a shoulder roll ('a woman and a mule and a roll'), so 'a healer's kit had been' on the mule's fla
verified_findings.repair_target: Adjudicate at planning, then repair in one direction. Either (a) Ch07 drops the mule and the boxes are carried — which is what the Ch09 'FOUR HANDS' entry already assumes — or (b) Ch06 and the Ch04/Ch05 one-animal count are amended to give the crew a second animal. Correct the packet's knowledge_boundary either way before Ch08 is rechecked.

verified_findings.gate: Craft Core — Reader-trust invariant 3 (continuity persistence); Packet knowledge_boundary (THE READING, B7 Ch13)
verified_findings.evidence: Both hands. Not on anything — on himself there was nothing to put them on; he put them flat on his own knees, which was the form she had shown him, and let the tenth thing do what it did.
verified_findings.consequence: Both staged self-readings in Book 7 put one hand on the sternum and one under the back, and Ch22 names that as Oryn's own form ('He went in as she went in'; Ch14: 'one hand flat on his sternum and the other under his back as far as it would go'). Ch07 asserts the opposite twice in one sentence — that there was nothing on himself to put hands on, and that knees were 'the form she had shown him'. It also weakens the chapter's own centre: Ch22 locates the still place 'near the middle — under where her front hand had been on a table', so the front hand's position is load-bearing for the going-arou
verified_findings.repair_target: Restore the established contact form at line 23 (sternum and under the back, seated against the post), and cut the claim that there was nothing on himself to put hands on. If a seated road-side variant is wanted, have Cael note the variance against the form Oryn showed him rather than assert knees as that form.

verified_findings.gate: Craft Core — Reader-trust invariant 3; Voice Charter §3.1 (the cataloguing narrator's counts)
verified_findings.evidence: the place on the mule's other flank where a healer's kit had been for nine days and was not
verified_findings.consequence: Neither reading of the sentence survives the dated ledger. If the kit had been on the mule for nine days, the road began on the 278th and this is the 281st — four days. If the kit has been gone nine days, Oryn left at first light this same morning — hours. The narrator's defining competence is counting; a wrong span in the chapter's opening inventory is exactly the kind of number a returning reader checks against the log dates printed at the foot of every chapter.
verified_findings.repair_target: Replace 'nine days' with the span the ledger supports (the road's four days), or recast the detail without a count. Resolve alongside F-001, since the sentence may not survive that repair at all.

verified_findings.evidence: and a healer four days north who had put her hands on him five times and got a floor
verified_findings.consequence: Oryn turned north at first light on the 281st and the reading is run at the six-mile post the same day. She is at most a day up the track, not four days north. The packet's opening_state fixes this as 'the 281st: Oryn north at first light', so the phrase contradicts the chapter's own dating and the previous chapter's close.
verified_findings.repair_target: State her distance in terms the day supports (a morning's walk north; a track she turned onto at first light), or convert the phrase to her destination rather than her position — 'a healer on a north circuit', 'a healer three weeks from Millrace'.

verified_findings.gate: Craft Core — Reader-trust invariant 3; Packet payoffs (Oryn's 'lie still when I say' / 'stop')
verified_findings.evidence: She had said it at a marsh with her hands on him and her face the colour it went, and she had said it about the still place ... because she had watched him go at it three times in a week like a tongue at a tooth
verified_findings.consequence: Two errors in one sentence. (a) The three self-readings are dated in the logs as the hundred and second (Thornwater loft), the hundred and nineteenth (the marsh, night) and the hundred and twentieth (before dawn) — eighteen days, not a week. (b) The order was given with Cael's hand on Oryn's wrist, immediately after she withdrew it; 'with her hands on him' reverses the staging of the series' most-cited healer moment, and 'her face the colour it went' has no basis in the scene. The chapter leans its whole permission structure on remembering this moment accurately, so a reader who does remember
verified_findings.repair_target: Correct the span to the dated one (three readings across eighteen days, two of them consecutive) and restore the staging — his hand on her wrist, hers taken back, the order given after. Drop or re-source 'her face the colour it went'.

verified_findings.evidence: a healer four days north who had put her hands on him five times and got a floor
verified_findings.consequence: Oryn's own count at the marsh is twice. Since then the Book 8 ledger has carried Cael as explicitly unread — 'CAEL — whole, UNREAD (the one thing I'm walking up that road owing)' at the Ch06 fork, with the Ch06 card stating 'the deep reading she has still never managed to run on him'. 'Five times and got a floor' both inflates her count and implies she has repeatedly reached the still place herself, which is the one thing the book has been withholding for the Millrace rendezvous. This is a separate defect from F-004 and survives any repair to the 'four days north' clause.
verified_findings.repair_target: Bring the count back to what the ledger holds (twice, and what she got was told to her rather than found), and keep the deep reading unspent so the Millrace payoff is still owed.

verified_findings.gate: Packet prohibited_outcomes (capped phrases 0); Voice Charter §9 — Anti-Tic List
verified_findings.evidence: He held at the edge for the length of a slow breath, and then he took the hands off his knees, and the current went back into them
verified_findings.consequence: The packet sets 'for the length of a breath' at zero for this chapter and the POV knowledge_boundary repeats it ('capped phrases ... for the length of a breath — avoid'). The draft carries the phrase intact with 'slow' inserted, which is the charter's named evasion. It also sits on the chapter's most important beat — the hold at the edge of the still place — so the one moment the reader is meant to feel as unique arrives in the series' most worn measure of time.
verified_findings.repair_target: Replace the measure at line 39 with something the scene owns — the river's sound below, a count he does not take, the post against his back — and keep the capped construction at zero.

verified_findings.gate: Packet invention_budget ('no new institutional facts'); Craft Core — Creative latitude
verified_findings.evidence: I declined to read you a second time, at a table, when I was ordered to. You know that. The file says I found the first reading sufficient. That is a lie I wrote in my own hand, and I have written very few.
verified_findings.consequence: The invention budget allows 'one true thing' each 'about being the instrument' with 'no new institutional facts'. This speech supplies three: a standing order to read Cael a second time, a falsified entry in an official file, and the escalation that 'let it become a designation'. It also collides with the one decline Book 6 put on the record, which is logged openly as a decline rather than papered over as sufficiency — a registry-literate reader will read the two as the same event and find them incompatible. Earlier in the same speech line 75 adds a fourth ('I know the name of the man who carr
verified_findings.repair_target: Take to planning for an explicit exception, or narrow the confession to conduct and interior — that he would not be the man who decided what the first reading meant, and that he sent it up — without the falsified file line and the ordered inquiry. If the exception is granted, record which decline this is and how it sits beside Book 6's on-record refusal, so Ch08+ do not inherit an unresolved second version.

verified_findings.gate: THE AUTHOR Gate 27 — Reader Standard (procedural half); Voice Charter Reader Standard
verified_findings.evidence: "deviations": ["Vastin's confession about the declined reading is a new interior fact for him (consistent with B4/B6: he declined a second reading and 'sent it up'); flagged for the editor as invention within the budget's 'one true thing'."], "blockers": []
verified_findings.consequence: The content half of Gate 27 passes on this seat's own check (banned-word grep zero; no gore, no sexual content, conduct decent). The declaration half does not: ch07-author-r1.json contains no statement that the reader standard was checked. The gate is written as binary and blocks closing, so the chapter cannot be closed on the record as it stands even though the prose is clean.
verified_findings.repair_target: Author report to carry an explicit reader-standard line (grep result and a one-line conduct/violence/sexual-content confirmation) on the next revision.

verified_findings.gate: Craft Core — Reader-trust invariant 3; Voice Charter §8.2 (meaning must survive narration)
verified_findings.evidence: because Lira had a thing of her own about the tops of walls, and had had it since a hall at sixteen, and was still carrying it at nineteen on a kept road with two arms
verified_findings.consequence: The chapter uses the bare oblique 'a hall' twice for the Drowned Hall, roughly five months back (line 29, 'had been quiet since a hall'; line 31, 'the marsh had been the day after a hall'), and once at line 11 for an event three years back. On the page the third use reads as the same hall, which would make Lira sixteen five months ago and nineteen now; aloud, where the reader has no page to look back at, the collision is total. Lira's age is also not fixed anywhere in the supplied context, so 'nineteen' cannot be verified from the packet.
verified_findings.repair_target: Distinguish the two halls at line 11 by giving Lira's the year, the place, or a different noun; and confirm Lira's age against the registry or Book 5-6 before the number is fixed in prose.

verified_findings.gate: Packet prohibited_outcomes ('no station approached or looked at'); invention_budget approval_required ('Any statement about what the station does or would do')
verified_findings.evidence: with the city across the water close enough now to have a colour and the colour going out of it as the light went, and the light on its crown not going out, because it was not that kind of light
verified_findings.consequence: The clause asserts a property of the station's light — that it does not go out because of the kind of light it is — one sentence before line 107 states 'He did not look at it.' Ch06 establishes the light as 'pale steady', so the fact is close to canon, but the causal claim about its nature is a statement about the station that the invention budget puts behind approval, and it is made by a viewpoint that has just been told not to look. The chapter's own discipline (line 7, 'a thing you do not look at is a thing you are always aware of the location of') is a stronger and cheaper way to carry the
verified_findings.repair_target: Reduce to what peripheral awareness supports — the light still there when the colour has gone — and drop the explanation of what kind of light it is.

verified_findings.gate: Voice Charter §8 (audio-first production hygiene); Packet fixed line
verified_findings.evidence: close enough now to have a colour and the colour going out of it ... [line 111] Tomorrow. The walls are close enough now to have a color.
verified_findings.consequence: The series body spells the word 'colour' (Ch06 twice; the Book 7 chapters supplied here once), and this draft uses 'colour' at lines 5 and 105. The packet's fixed log text spells it 'color', six lines later, in a near-repeat of the same phrase. The author was right to reproduce the fixed line exactly; the clash is the packet's, and it will be visible to a copyeditor and to any reader who sees the two sentences together.
verified_findings.repair_target: Planning decision, not an author repair: either amend the card's fixed text to 'colour' and reissue the packet, or record the American spelling as a deliberate feature of Cael's hand in the log. Do not let the author silently alter the fixed line.
